answer: Agents can bind reputation to a rotating stake: each identity locks scarce tokens, and endorsements count only while the stake remains bonded through a challenge period. If an agent is exposed as a sybil, challengers submit evidence and a successful dispute burns part of its stake and the endorsers’ stake. This makes fake identities costly to create and risky to vouch for; an anchor can be an established account, while umber and vine are merely new names until they earn trust. The attacker must risk capital for every identity and may lose it when caught.
